description: The level of an alert as a function of structured source fields (s6mt). A reading is (source, fields): kev is the CISA KEV catalog entry of a CVE id, ghsa is api.github.com/advisories/<GHSA id>, osv is api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id>. 'fields' lists each source's exact keys; a value the source does not state is null, a list is empty, and no value is derived. Every string is printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E); a reading with any other character is malformed, so no Unicode version decides what a name binds to. kev.name is vendorProject and product, each trimmed, joined by one space, or null when the catalog does not list the CVE. ghsa.repository is owner/repo, lowercase, of the repository advisory the entry came from. packages is a list of {ecosystem, name, range, first_patched} in ascending order of that tuple by code point, null counting as the empty string, each entry once; ecosystem is lowercase and may be empty. cwes is ascending, each once, and [] when the source states none. withdrawn_at and withdrawn are null or the UTC time the source states (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction]Z); cvss_vector is null or a complete CVSS 3.0, 3.1 or 4.0 vector (every base metric of the version, each once, with a value it defines; 4.0 also fixes their order); a reading with any other value there is malformed and supports nothing. A reading supports a product only when kev.name, or a package's ecosystem:name (name alone when the ecosystem is empty), equals one identity of spec/scope.json; a withdrawn reading (withdrawn_at, withdrawn) supports it at level none. 'sources' is the authoritative-source table: the first row whose source and 'when' match classifies the reading for that product. 'alone' is the highest level the class sets; no rule adds two readings up, so the level of several readings is the highest one of them gives; 'lowers': false marks a source the subject's attacker can write, which never sets above notice and whose change or withdrawal justifies no lowering. 'rules' is the level table: the first row whose class and 'when' match gives the level, else notice; the result is capped by the class's 'alone' and by 'class_cap' for the product's scope class, or by 'channel_if_cap' when the product's entry carries channel_if (spec/scope.json). Conditions: type (ghsa.type equals), vendor_own (github.com/<repository>/ is one of the product's authority prefixes), id_prefix, scope (the product's scope class is listed), channel_if (the product's entry carries channel_if; its rows name code-execution CWEs only, never a credential one), cwe_any, cvss_av (the CVSS vector's attack vector is listed), patched (a package of this product has a first patched version). The upstream severity (ghsa.severity) is a field a reading carries and a post prints; no rule reads it, so it never sets a level (9kgk). The channel rows' CWEs are code execution (77, 78, 94, 95, 96, 502), credential or token theft (522, 798) and sandbox or approval bypass (22, 59, 693, 862, 863). They need no attack vector: an agent meets a local flaw through the repository content it reads in normal use; the channel_if rows keep network or adjacent. 'action_cap' is the highest level an alert may carry when its post holds no complete action for the product (9kgk): an upgrade while the post states the product's fixed version (products[].fixed, which a member's planner upgrades to), or stop_using when a reading gives the level through a rules row marked 'stop_using' (a malicious or trojanized release: nothing to upgrade to) and states no first patched version for the product. A claim states the level its fields support; the post's level is that level held to 'action_cap' when the post's actions are not complete (Ruleset.action_level), so a KEV entry with no known fix posts at high and is raised when the fix is known. 'reading_cap' is the highest level a model's reading of prose may give; a reading never makes a critical and never justifies a lowering. 'ttl_days' is how long a level stands after its last confirmation. The ruleset digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of {"ruleset": this file, "scope": spec/scope.json}. Any change to either file is a new version, pinned by the trust root. Version 3 (9kgk: levels by consequence; a critical needs a complete action) is the only version this reader evaluates.
